violation_type.title: AP Parental Communication - Injury Requires Treatment by Health Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.307(b)(1))
violation_type.short_title: AP Parental Communication - Injury Requires Treatment by Health Care Professional or Hospitalization
violation_type.typical_finding: Staff did not notify the parents of a child who received an injury while in care.

finding_variants.text: Staff did not notify the parents of a child who received an injury while in care.
The operation failed to report to a parent (before the parent picked the child up and at pick-up) that a child was injured in care.

Based on information gathered during the investigation, a child received an injury while in care, was immediately unable to put weight on their leg and continued to be unable to put weight on the leg while outside on the playground including when the parent picked up at the end of the day an hour after the accident occurred.
A parent was not immediately contacted when blood was found in child's diaper.
This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and found to be deficient. A child received an injury that later required medical attention and the parent was not immediately notified.

This standard was found to be out of compliance when staff did not immediately notify a parent of a serious injury requiring medical treatment. The staff delayed 25 minutes before contacting the parent or other emergency contact.

AP Parental Communication - Injury Requires Treatment by Health Care Professional or Hospitalization: A child sustained a broken femur.  The caregiver was unaware of the injury.  Medical stated this type of injury is immediately noticeable and the child would cry.  The child did cry and the staff saw similar signs of the child's constipation. However, the child could not bear weight which not a symptom of his constipation.  The parent was not informed of this other symptom.  The child was crying from the end of nap to pick up at 5:55pm.
